tasks.short: Inspect, sort and adjust packaged products

steps.what: Read the current product weight and grading specification
Sort, grade, weigh and inspect products against the specification
Adjust product contents or dimensions to meet limits

tasks.design: Retain physical sorting, weighing, inspection and adjustment. Check whether the existing {DOCS} specification is already at the workstation; no retrieval saving is attributed to a view the operator already has.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hands must handle products and correct actual contents.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital specifications can support the work but do not replace its physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Judging defects that measurements alone do not describe.
tasks.human_edge: Notice damage, contamination and misleading scale readings.
tasks.altitude: No change in duties or authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: product weighing and content adjustment involve physical handling; native scale runtime is not operator labour.

assumptions: Focal boundary is manual sample or product inspection and correction. Shares are provisional, not measured.

Production planning supplies the order; quality staff supply approved product identifier, weight limits, units and grade criteria in the existing specification. The operator reads it in s1; missing limits require manual clarification, not guessed values.
The existing scale displays measurements; no new automated measurement capture or robot is proposed. Existing automatic checkweighing earns no labour saving.

An inspection tally or quality report is not established here. If actually required, count its first entry separately and assess native forms before estimating savings. Do not add a log with no reader.
No change means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Whether an actual quality tally is required
Whether manual weighing or existing checkweighing predominates
research_questions: Observe product handling and any actual quality entry separately.

already_counted.description: Specification reading, handling and correction remain fully retained.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All focal work remains. Even readily available digital limits do not remove the operator's measurement or adjustment, and no new recording baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Stop faulty equipment, clear jams and report malfunctions

steps.what: Stop the machine and make the jam area safe
Clear permitted jams and reset only when safe
Enter observed malfunction and clearance outcome in the maintenance report
Check final fault report and supervisor destination
outputs: final checked fault report and destination

steps.what: Send the checked malfunction report to the supervisor
inputs: final checked fault report and destination

tasks.design: In the maintenance-management category {OTHER}, test a native machine-linked fault form that carries the existing machine identifier into the report. The operator writes the symptoms, checks the final report, and sends it to the supervisor; physical stop, clearance and reset work remain unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Machine identity can be repeatedly typed while the fault description needs direct observation.
tasks.enabler_now: A native machine-linked form can remove identifier re-entry without diagnosing the fault.
tasks.still_hard: Safe isolation, knowing when not to reset, and accurate reporting of unresolved hazards.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the jam requires qualified maintenance rather than another restart.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less report entry; unchanged stop and escalation responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: maintenance systems can prefill a machine identifier from an existing asset context while retaining operator symptom entry.

assumptions: Focal boundary includes stopping, permitted clearance/reset and the actual supervisor fault report. This graph models an existing maintenance-system reporting branch; verify that branch before using these provisional shares.

Maintenance staff already maintain asset identifier and supervisor routing. The operator selects the machine and enters fault time, symptoms, clearance and remaining unsafe condition in s3; no sensor diagnosis or unpriced transcript is assumed. Wrong asset context is manually corrected in retained s3 and checked in s4.

Only repeated machine identifier entry, 10% of s3, is removed. Report wording and ordinary same-system saving remain fully retained and ungated within s3. The separate send is a real internal handoff, fully retained rather than treated as a large save.

s4 binds the completed report and supervisor destination for s5; edits void that approval. Urgent verbal safety escalation must still happen immediately; where it is additional rather than part of safe handling, add its actual time and reweight.
No changes to machine controls, guards or restart permissions are proposed.
unknowns: Whether reports currently use a maintenance system or verbal supervisor handoff
research_questions: Does native asset context remove retyping without hiding symptom or safety information?

already_counted.description: Fault description, asset corrections and final verification remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Operator checks saved machine context after equipment or routing changes.

approvals.approved_version: s4 final checked fault report and named supervisor destination; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; identifier reuse removes 14*0.10=1.4 hours, less 0.3 upkeep gives 1.1 net. Cautious case: a shared workstation requires fresh asset selection and only 0.4 hours of retyping disappear, giving 0.1 net; all safety and send work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe packaging operations against quality standards

steps.what: Read the active packaging standard and approved reference sample
Observe machine operations and judge filled or packaged product conformity

tasks.design: Keep direct machine and product observation, using the current {DOCS} standard and reference sample. Native specification presentation is already available in this boundary; no new camera inspection or fabricated quality record is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conformity includes changing physical conditions and defects beyond a fixed image.
tasks.enabler_now: Document access supports interpretation but does not shorten the required observation.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting emerging filling and sealing problems in time.
tasks.human_edge: Combine appearance, sound and machine behaviour to recognise abnormal production.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: observing a running packaging line remains physical work unless a validated sensing and inspection installation replaces a defined observation.

assumptions: Boundary is observation against existing standards; stopping and malfunction reporting belong to task 3129 and must not be counted again. Shares are provisional.

Quality staff supply the approved product/packaging revision and criteria, and planning supplies the active order. The operator checks them in s1; missing or conflicting versions require manual clarification.
A current standard is already accessible. Native views therefore have no established removed navigation here. No new structured capture is introduced.

Check actual quality tally requirements before deployment; none is established by this observation task, so no trailing log is invented. If actual first entries exist, split them and test native forms.
No introduced system entails zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Whether an existing line inspection system already performs some checks
Whether the task includes an actual operator quality tally
research_questions: Which specific observations would a validated inspection system replace, and which would remain?

already_counted.description: Reading criteria and live observation remain in full.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 100 focal hours remain. Availability of the standard does not replace direct observation; no inspection-installation performance or administrative baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the production line for jams and adhesive failures

steps.what: Monitor the production line for pile-ups, jams and glue failures

tasks.design: Retain live monitoring of movement and adhesive performance. Existing machine alarms have no new operator-labour saving; a new sensing installation would need its own defect-specific validation before changing this graph.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pile-ups and poorly bonded packs are physical and may develop between machine alarms.
tasks.enabler_now: No established software change replaces the operator's observation in this boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing harmless accumulation from a developing jam and spotting weak adhesion.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unusual movement, sound and pack condition together.
tasks.altitude: The operator continues watching the line.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: line monitoring can include physical defects that existing alarms do not reliably identify.

assumptions: Focal boundary is watching the line, not stopping, clearing or reporting the discovered malfunction; task 3129 owns those actions. No duplicate labour is saved.

No record write, message, scheduled report or separate lookup is established for continuous watching. If a real exception entry belongs here rather than 3129, count it once and test the existing native form before estimating benefit.
No structured input, new model or new sensor feed is assumed. Existing automatic alarm runtime is not labour.
The 100% allocation represents the task boundary, not a measured duration. No system change means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether any actual exception entry is owned by this task
research_questions: Observe adhesive failures missed by existing alarms before proposing additional sensing.

already_counted.description: Physical line monitoring remains fully retained.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The work is live observation and remains 100%. No invented line log or new sensor capability is used to claim a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical operation and quality judgement stay with the operator; only small fault-report identifier entry is reduced.
skills_to_grow: Check packaging criteria against the active product revision
role.ambitious_version: No expanded production responsibility follows from a small report-entry change.
